_comment:
Hand-curated orientations for spots where the geometric algorithm cannot resolve the seaward bearing. Applied by pipeline/enrich.py between Algorithm 1 (orientation) and Algorithm 2 (swell window), so the orientation-derived fallback builds arcs against the correct value. Treated as authoritative — overrides both the algorithmic result and LLM verification. Match by exact spot name.

WHEN TO ADD AN ENTRY:
- Great Lakes spots (GSHHG L1 lumps the lakes with land — orientation returns null)
- Complex harbors, jetties, rivermouths where the coastline normal misrepresents the actual break geometry
- Barrier-island spots whose Nominatim geocode landed on the bay side and whose automatic 180° hemisphere flip didn't cover it
- Spots in Alaska / Guam / territories not covered by the region hemisphere table

FIELDS:
- orientation_deg (required, 0-359): the seaward-facing bearing. 0=N, 90=E, 180=S, 270=W. This is the direction the rider looks when facing the incoming swell.
- source (optional): short attribution — 'local knowledge', 'surf-forecast.com manual check', 'OSM way heading', etc.
- notes (optional): any disambiguation that matters (e.g. 'Pier points straight offshore', 'Break faces the reef pass rather than the beach', or flagging that the spot's coord looks wrong and needs a fix in spot_coord_fixes.json).

NULL-ORIENTATION SPOTS (DQ-5) AND WHY THE ARC MIDPOINT IS THE SOURCE:
A null orientation_deg is a CORRECTNESS fault, not a cosmetic one. nwps_stars returns all None when orientation is null, and apply_nwps_overrides skips an hour whose stars are None, so a spot placed on the nwps tier with a null orientation silently keeps its orientation-path rating every hour of every cycle — the NWPS override never fires and nothing reports a failure. Shell Beach (North) was in exactly that state.
For such spots the value here is the MIDPOINT OF THE WIDEST SWELL WINDOW ARC. The obvious alternative is a derived shore normal, and it was TESTED AND REJECTED: _shore_seaward_bearings in forecast/nwps_nearshore.py infers a seaward bearing from the NWPS land mask by taking the opposite of the bearing to the nearest MASKED cell. For Rockpile (Laguna) it returns 230 deg, within 10 deg of the arc midpoint, because the nearest land is 1.17 km away and the coast is locally straight. For Shell Beach (North) it returns 114 deg — 108 deg away and very nearly OPPOSITE the true facing — because the nearest masked cell is 4.79 km off and the spot sits inside San Luis Obispo Bay, where land wraps around it on three sides and 'nearest land' stops meaning 'shoreward'. The mask method therefore fails precisely in the bays and harbors where an orientation is most likely to be missing in the first place, which makes it useless exactly where it would be needed. NO RUNTIME DERIVATION WAS ADDED: two hand-checked values are better than a rule that fails in bays.
NOTE ON PRECEDENCE, which decides whether an entry here has any effect at all: enrich.py applies this name-keyed file FIRST and then the slug-keyed spot_orientations.json, so a slug row there BEATS anything written here (see _load_spot_orientations' own docstring: 'a slug match here beats every other source'). An entry in this file is only effective when that slug has NO row in spot_orientations.json — which is why the two promoted entries below say the slug row was removed. Both spots added for DQ-5 were absent from BOTH files, so these two entries are effective as written. AS OF 2026-08-17 THIS CAVEAT IS HISTORICAL: no name in this file has a slug row in spot_orientations.json, so every entry here is effective. BU-17 promoted the 21 live disagreements (plus Sebastian Inlet and Rincon, which agreed) by writing the reviewed value here and deleting the slug row, and the 18 remaining collisions were Great Lakes spots in excluded_spots.json whose entries were deleted from both files. pipeline/tests/test_orientation_override_collision.py fails if a collision is ever reintroduced, so the precedence order in enrich.py is no longer load-bearing for these values.

IB Jetty.notes: Jetty points SW into the Pacific

Gooch's Beach.notes: Atlantic-facing beach with a SE bend toward Wells Bay

Avalon NJ.notes: MANUAL ORIENTATION APPLIED BUT COORDS LOOK WRONG — (40.82, -74.32) is inland NJ near Livingston, not the actual Avalon at ~(39.10, -74.72). Needs entry in spot_coord_fixes.json to correct lat/lng before enrichment can compute buoy/tide.

Ocean Isle Beach.notes: Island runs E-W; faces south into Long Bay

Sunset Beach NC.source: Brunswick County, NC (adjacent to Ocean Isle)

Florence South Jetty.source: Oregon coast at the Siuslaw River mouth
Florence South Jetty.notes: Jetty faces west into the open Pacific

Charlestown Town Beach.source: South Rhode Island coast / Block Island Sound

Indicators Rincon.notes: Just N of Domes; faces WNW

Marias Rincon.notes: Maria's faces slightly N of W

Domes Beach Aguadilla.notes: Aguadilla coast curves from W-facing (Rincon) to N-facing; Domes here faces NW

Playa Kikita.source: North coast of Puerto Rico (Manatí area)

Kamea Meha.notes: Coord near San Juan's Condado/Isla Verde; faces N

The Room.source: North coast of Puerto Rico (Isabela area)

Sebastian Inlet.notes: Optimal swell from NE (45°) but beach faces E

Rincon.notes: Optimal swell from WNW (290°) wraps around point. Cove faces SSW.

North Jetty.notes: Human-verified NE facing into the jetty pocket at Sebastian Inlet. Geometric computation yields ~111 deg because raycast sees the open beach ~72 m away, not the pocket. Promoted from spot_orientations.json (bulk cache) so a re-seed cannot overwrite it.

Jetty Park Cocoa Beach.source: verification_notes: 'the actual wave-facing direction at the south jetty wall is closer to true east (~90 deg)'
Jetty Park Cocoa Beach.notes: South side of Port Canaveral inlet jetty. Coastline-polygon computation gives 131 deg (SE); human structural observation of the jetty wall, promoted from spot_orientations.json bulk cache.

Rockpile (Laguna).source: arc midpoint — swell window 157-283 deg, span 130, midpoint 220
Rockpile (Laguna).notes: DQ-5: orientation_deg was NULL, which left the spot unplaced. SW-facing, consistent with neighbouring Orange County spots at 210-230 deg. The mask-derived seaward bearing agrees here (230 deg, within 10) because the nearest land is 1.17 km off and the coast is locally straight — it is Shell Beach (North) that shows why the mask method cannot be trusted in general. No row in spot_orientations.json, so this value is the effective one; if a bulk re-seed ever adds that slug, remove it or this is silently overridden.

Shell Beach (North).source: arc midpoint — swell window 185-259 deg, span 78, midpoint 222
Shell Beach (North).notes: DQ-5: orientation_deg was NULL while the spot was ALREADY PLACED on the nwps tier, so its NWPS override silently never fired and it kept the orientation-path rating every hour of every cycle. SW-facing, consistent with neighbouring San Luis Obispo County spots at 210-230 deg. The mask-derived seaward bearing is 114 deg here — 108 deg out and nearly opposite — because the spot sits inside San Luis Obispo Bay with the nearest masked cell 4.79 km away; this is the case that rejected a runtime derivation. No row in spot_orientations.json, so this value is the effective one.
